The varying widths of the confidence intervals reflect a growing degree of uncertainty as the forecast horizon extends. While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain specific risks or unforeseen events could still push the actual results outside these boundaries. These might include sudden and severe macroeconomic shocks, such as an unexpected interest rate hike or a sharp downturn in economic growth, significant geopolitical developments like new conflicts or trade wars, or major industry-specific disruptions like a technological breakthrough or a regulatory overhaul. Furthermore, "black swan" events—highly improbable, high-impact occurrences that are difficult to predict—always pose a risk of rendering even carefully constructed forecasts inaccurate by introducing entirely new market dynamics.
